correctness.rationale: Homma–Kim normal form identifies filling quartics with M_3(F2)/F2 I and smoothness with irreducible cubic characteristic polynomial, det A=det(A+I)=1. Counting GL3(2)=168, 48 irreducible matrices and A~A+I gives 24 smooth classes. Each embedded F8 contains three nontrivial cosets, hence eight Singer pencils. Fixing one Singer generator, the other 21 smooth cosets split into three conjugation orbits of seven and have no smooth sum with it; this proves no cross-Singer pencil. Stabilizers 7 (curve), 21 (pencil), no 3D all-smooth subspace, and tangent covectors form the 3 lines through each rational point. Independent exhaustive 512-matrix/coset/class/group checks established 24 smooth classes and exactly eight edge-disjoint smooth triples; finite enumeration is exhaustive for this F2 domain, while irreducible-matrix smoothness uses a published theorem.
residual_risks: Computational examples alone do not establish quantification beyond checked finite parameters; the analytical or finite-exhaustive proof is separately evaluated.

originality.rationale: Homma–Kim 2009 already classifies individual nonsingular degree-four filling curves, their matrix representatives and automorphisms. Asgarli–Ghioca 2022 proves a general pencil existence result only under a sufficiently large-field condition, not this q=2 classification. The new incidence classification across smooth quartics (eight Singer all-smooth F2 pencils, cross-Singer obstruction, no smooth 3-space) was not found in inspected sources. It is a motivated complete smallest-field finite geometry fact, though an older Fano/Singer matrix spread interpretation might imply it.
residual_risks: Finite-geometry literature on Singer cyclic spreads in M3(F2)/scalars might contain the exact additive-triple incidence under different notation.
The independent finite certificate does not replace verifying the published smoothness equivalence for all geometric points; that equivalence was checked as a published theorem.
